The factual matrix of the case are as follows:-
The complainant and the accused are family friends and have acquaintance with each other and out of such acquaintance, the accused in the first week of February 2015,
approached the complainant and requested to pay a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- as handloan so as to enable the accused to improve the business being run by the accused with her brother Mr. K.A. Anji Raju, under the name and style of "GANGA FASSION N' STYLE" which is situated near Krishna Theatre, Basavanapura Main road, K.R. C.C.No.54360/2015 Puram, Bengaluru - 560036 and thereby promised and assured the complainant to repay the same within three months from the said date.

Pursuant to the approach made by the accused, the complainant with an intention to help the accused to improve their business had paid a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- to the accused in the second week of February 2015.

Pursuant to receipt of the amount as aforesaid and inspite of lapse of three months as agreed, the accused failed and neglected to repay the amount payable to the complainant and as such, having no other alternative the complainant voluntarily approached the accused and requested to repay the amount payable.

Upon such request, the accused on one pretext or the other had been escaping from her liability, thereafter on persistent demands made by the complainant, the accused in discharge of her debt and liability issued a cheque bearing No.030389 dated 03.06.2015 drawn on Vijaya Bank, K.R. Puram Branch, Bengaluru-560036 and thereby promised and assured the complainant that the said cheque would C.C.No.54360/2015 be duly honored on the date of its presentation.

The complainant presented the said cheque for encashment on 08.06.2015 through her banker Vijaya Bank, K.R. Puram Branch, Bengaluru-560036, but it came to be dishonored for the reason "funds insufficient" vide endorsement dated 11.06.2015.

Thereafter,
the complainant issued legal notice on 24.06.2015 to the accused calling upon the accused to pay the cheque amount.
The notice sent to the accused's residential address was duly served on the accused and the notice sent to the address where she is running her business returned unserved with a shara "Not Claimed".
Hence, the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

3. Based on the complaint, the sworn statement affidavit, the documents etc., the court took cognizance of an offence punishable under Sec.138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act by following the guidelines of Apex Court issued in Indian Bank C.C.No.54360/2015 Association case and ordered to register a criminal case against the accused for the offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

4. In pursuance of summons, the accused appeared through her counsel, she was enlarged on court bail, further, substance of plea was recorded, the accused pleaded not guilty and she claimed to be tried.
In order to prove her case, the complainant got examined herself as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P9 and got marked Ex.P10 by way of confrontation during the cross-examination of DW1.

Upon closure of complainant's side evidence, the court examined the accused U/s 313 of Cr.P.C, the accused denied the incriminating materials appearing against her and the accused got examined M.A. Anuradha vs A. Revathi on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166066156/

The following points would arise for my consideration:-
1.
Whether the complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused has committed an o/p/u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act?
What Order?

7. My findings on the above points are as follows;
Point No1: In the Affirmative, Point No.2: As per final order, for the following, R E A S O N S 8.
POINT No.1: I have gone through the materials available on record.
The learned counsel for the complainant has argued reiterating complaint allegations during his arguments.

The counsel for the complainant has argued that the accused had borrowed Rs.6,00,000/- agreeing to repay it within three months and towards repayment of the said loan the accused had issued the cheque in question in favour of the complainant and it came to be dishonored for the reason "Funds insufficient" and inspite of intimating the said fact through legal notice dated 09.08.2021, she did not pay the cheque amount and hence, the accused is liable to be convicted for C.C.No.54360/2015 the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
9.

The complainant, who has been examined as PW1, has reiterated the facts stated in her complaint in her chief examination also and in addition to it, she has produced Ex.P1 to 10.
10.

Ex.P1 is the cheque bearing No.030389 dated 08.06.2015 drawn on Vijaya Bank, K.R. Puram,
Bangalore, for Rs.6,00,000/- said to have been issued by the accused in favour of the complainant.
Ex.P2 is the return memo dated 11.06.2015 said to have been issued by the complainant's banker which goes to show that the cheque in question was dishonored for the reason "Funds insufficient".

Ex.P3 is the copy of the legal notice dated 24.06.2015 said to have been sent by the complainant to the accused intimating the fact of dishonour of the cheque to the accused and demanding payment of cheque amount.
Ex . P4
is the postal receipts.

is the postal acknowledgment C.C.No.54360/2015 which goes to show that the statutory notice sent to the accused was duly served.
Ex . P6
is the returned postal cover.
Ex . P7
is the reply notice dated 01.07.2015 said to have been issued by accused to the legal notice of the complainant.

Ex.P8 is the certified copy of the sale deed dated 08.05.2013 said to have been executed by Sri. H. Murgendrappa, Nisarga M, and M.
Bhoomika

represented by her minor guardian father Sri. H. Murgendrappa in favour of Sri. S.
Kumar and Smt. Sowmyashree G for valuable consideration of Rs.30,30,000/- in respect of the property mentioned in the schedule therein
. Ex.P9 is the Bank challan.

Ex.P10 is the copy of the reply notice which is at Ex.P7.
11.

It is relevant to mention here that during the cross-examination of PW1, the learned counsel for the accused has suggested that the complainant got created Ex.P1 since the contents of the cheque in question are in the handwriting of her brother and further suggested in her cross-examination that M.A. Anuradha vs A. Revathi on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166066156/
4 the C.C.No.54360/2015 accused has not signed Ex.P1 and as such, the bank endorsement is given as per Ex.P2.
Further the accused, who has been examined as DW1, has categorically stated in her cross examination that the signature on the Ex.P1 cheque in question does not belong to her.
The accused though disputed her signature on Ex.P1, she has not adduced sufficient oral and documentary evidence to establish it.

Further the accused during her chief examination itself at para No.15 has categorically stated that she gave to the complainant two blank signed cheques, one blank signed stamp paper, one blank signed cheque of the surety for the purpose of taking the bid amount of the chit she subscribed with the complainant.

Further during the cross-examination of PW1 the learned counsel for the accused though made the above said suggestions, he has put a suggestion to the witness that she saying to the accused and her younger brother that she had own prize in the chit and obtained the cheque in question as security from the accused.

It is relevant to mention here that nobody C.C.No.54360/2015 would issue blank cheque as security without there being signature of the account holder and further the averments made in the chief examination of the accused itself goes to show that it was a signed cheque issued by the accused.
In view of the contradictions in the above said suggestions and the defence of the accused, the defence of the accused that Ex.P1(a) is not her signature cannot be accepted.
Further it is not the case of the accused that the cheque in question does not pertain to her account.

Such being the case, it is relevant to mention here that when the accused has admitted the issuance of the cheque and her signature on it, the initial presumption as contemplated U/S 139 of the N.I Act has to be raised by the court in favour of the complainant, however the accused is entitled to rebut the said presumptions as held in the case of Sri Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan by the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in AIR 2010 SC 1898.

sentences.text: . Once the presumption U/S 139 and 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is raised, it is for the accused to rebut the said presumption by adducing cogent evidence in support of his defence.

It is the specific defence of the accused that she subscribed to a chit of Rs.5,00,000/- having monthly premium of Rs.20,000/- with the complainant on the representation of one Smt. Nithu @ Niveditha and likewise Smt. Jaya, Smt. Sujatha, Smt. Shanthamma and Smt. Lakshmamma had also subscribed a chit each with the complainant and that the said chit was commenced on 01.07.2013 and in the month of October 2014, she bid the chit for Rs.4,40,000/- by leaving Rs.60,000/- and that for the purpose of taking the said bid amount of the chit she gave two signed blank cheques, one signed blank paper, one signed blank cheque of the surety to the complainant in the presence of above said Smt. Jaya, Smt. Sujatha and Smt. Lakshmamma on 05.10.2014, but the complainant failed to give her the bid amount even after collecting the above said documents and even C.C.No.54360/2015 after taking five months time.

The accused has further taken a defence that on 19.03.2014 during Ugadi festival she insisted the complainant to make immediate payment of the bid amount or otherwise told her that she would lodge a complaint and thereafter, on 29.03.2015,
the complainant along with her daughter Smt. Nisarga and her son-in-law Sri. Mukund came to her residence and beaten her with hands and proclaimed that they have paid Rs.1,00,000/- to the police Inspector Sanjeevappa of K.R. Puram police station out of said amount of Rs.4,40,000/- and he had assured them that he would not receive complaint against them and further the complainant has also stated to the accused that the Inspector has advised them to file a complaint by making use of the above said blank cheques and documents of the accused if the accused approaches the police or M.A. Anuradha vs A. Revathi on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166066156/
5 the court and by the said threats, the accused was totally scared and hence, she did not lodge any complaint to the police.

sentences.text: It is relevant to mention here that the accused has failed to elicit C.C.No.54360/2015 anything favourable in her favour in respect of the above said defence during the cross-examination of PW1 from her mouth.
Further the accused though stated that she had subscribed the above said chit, she did not adduce any documentary evidence in support of it.

Further the accused even failed to bring before this Court any other members of chit who were said to have subscribed chits with the complainant and further the accused even did not examine either Smt. Jaya or Smt. Sujatha or Smt. Lakshmamma or Smt. Shanthamma who were said to be present while the accused issuing the above said blank cheques and documents to the complainant on 05.10.2014 for the purpose of collecting the bid amount.

Further it is relevant to mention here that even till today the accused did not take any legal action against the complainant either for receiving the bid amount from her or for getting the above said blank documents handed over to the complainant and the story stated by the accused for her failure to take any such action is also baseless as she did not adduce C.C.No.54360/2015 any cogent oral and documentary evidence to establish the said facts.

It is relevant to mention here that no prudent woman would keep quite without taking any such legal action when she has not received the bid amount and though received such threatenings by the complainant and her son-in-law and daughter.

Further in para No.13 of her defence the accused has stated that the chit was for Rs.5,00,000/- and there were 20 members consisting of monthly premium of Rs.20,000/- for a term of 20 months and as against the said fact in para No.14 she has stated that the chit amount was for Rs.5,00,000/- and the monthly premium was Rs.20,000/- and the term was 25 months.

Further it is relevant to mention here that the accused though denied that there was any friendship with the complainant, she has not denied the acquaintance with the complainant as could be ascertained from the facts stated in her chief examination.

Further the accused in her reply notice at Ex.P10 at para No.6 has categorically stated that the complainant was supposed to give her bid amount C.C.No.54360/2015 of Rs.3,40,000/-
contrary to her chief examination that the amount supposed to be given by the complainant as claimed by the accused is Rs.4,40,000/-.

Further para No.14 of Ex.P10 goes to show that the accused had categorically stated that she would prosecute the complainant for the offences punishable under Sections.457, 468, 471 and 420 read with Section.120 and 34 of the I.P.C.

If for a moment the story of the accused for failure to take any legal action against the complainant in view of the threatenings made by the complainant and her family members is believed, what prevented the accused to take any legal action against the complainant from the date of the reply notice as stated in para.14 of the reply notice at Ex.P14 till this day cannot be ascertained and the reasons are best known to the accused herself.

Making firm denial of the case of the complainant and issuance of reply notice at the earliest point of time itself is not sufficient to believe the defence of the accused for the discussion made above.
It is further relevant to mention here that the accused has taken another defence that the complainant has no financial capacity to lend the alleged money to her.

At the first instance, the said defence itself is not at all maintainable in view of her specific defence regarding subscription of the chit and issuance of the above stated documents as security towards the bid amount.
The accused cannot take two different defences which are quite contradictory.

However, it is relevant to mention M.A. Anuradha vs A. Revathi on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166066156/
6 here that though the accused has disputed the financial capacity of the complainant, in her chief examination at para No.19 itself has categorically stated that she was very poor and doing tailoring work in the name and style of 'Gagan Fashions' and eking out her livelihood and her brother was an unemployed graduate and at the relevant point of time, he was doing business of recharging mobile currency and was earning Rs.100/- to Rs.150/- per day.

sentences.text: The said facts itself supports the case of the complainant about the need the accused had in relation to money.

Further it is relevant to C.C.No.54360/2015 mention here that during the cross-examination of PW1, no doubt, the complainant has admitted regarding filing of a cheque bounce case against one Mousin Shariff in C.C.No.53895/2014 and also admitted the documents produced by the accused pertaining to the said case which are marked at Ex.D11 to Ex.D21.
It is also true that the PW1 has admitted about filing another complaint by her against Sri. Anjiraju who is the brother of the accused.
It is relevant to mention here that the loan alleged to have been lent in both the said cases is Rs.6,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- in February 2015 and in the year 2012 respectively.

Merely because the complainant had filed the above said two complaints and has filed the present complaint against the accused is not sufficient to hold that the complainant had no financial capacity to lend the alleged money since it is the defence of the accused only that she had subscribed a chit of Rs.5,00,000/- with her and no prudent man would subscribe a chit for such a higher amount when the person conducting the chit has no financial capacity C.C.No.54360/2015 to pay it.
Further PW1 has categorically stated in her cross-examination that she had savings and had sale consideration of Rs.30,20,000/- received from sale of the site.
The complainant has also produced the copy of the said sale deed which is marked at Ex.

P8. The said document goes to show that it has been executed by the husband of the complainant Sri. H. Murugendrappa and his children in favour of one Sri. Kumar S. and his wife for the total sale consideration of Rs.30,30,000/- on 08.05.2013 and the said document at page No.3 further goes to show that out of the said sale consideration, Rs.15,00,000/- was paid in cash on 28.02.2013,
Rs.5,30,000/- in cash on the date of the said document and remaining amount of Rs.10,00,000/-
on 07.05.2013 through cheque.
Further PW1 in her cross-examination has categorically stated that the said site was in her husband's name and that her husband had given her Rs.30,20,000/- on the day of execution of Ex.P8.

Further the alleged loan said to have been lent in the second week of February 2015 and the recitals of Ex.P8 coupled with the above said C.C.No.54360/2015 statements of the PW1 categorically goes to show that the complainant had sufficient money in her hands to lend the alleged money.

Further the complainant has also categorically stated that she had salary income from her profession as Teacher till 2008 and that her husband used to get salary of Rs.40,000/- to Rs.45,000/- per month after 2012 from his profession as Assistant Traffic Supervisor in BMTC and there is nothing on record which would go contrary to the said statements of the complainant.

Merely because the complainant did not produce the I.T.R. pertaining to her husband and that her husband has not shown the above said transaction of sale in his I.T.R. is not sufficient to hold that the complainant had no financial capacity to pay the alleged money to the accused.

Further the non production of the chit in which the complainant stated that she might have made a writing for having lent the alleged money to the accused is also not a ground to believe the entire defence of the accused as it is not the case of the accused that she had executed any such writings in C.C.No.54360/2015 favour of the complainant.

From the above discussion, it is crystal clear that the accused even failed to prove her defence that the complainant had no financial capacity to lend the alleged money to the accused at the relevant point of time.

As such, in the above facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the categorical opinion the above said citations relied M.A. Anuradha vs A. Revathi on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166066156/
7 upon by the learned counsel for the accused in support of the said defence do not help the accused either to rebut the presumptions available in favour of the complainant or to hold that the accused has taken a probable defence.

sentences.text:
As such, considering the entire materials on record, in my opinion,
the accused has failed to rebut the presumptions available in favour of the complainant by adducing cogent oral and documentary evidence and even to raise a probable defence and on the other hand, I am of the opinion that the complainant has proved her case beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused has committed offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.

Hence, I am of the opinion that the C.C.No.54360/2015 accused has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
14.

It is relevant to mention here that the accused having issued cheque at Ex.P1 in favour of the complainant has failed to pay the cheque amount and hence, the complainant is to be suitably compensated for the delay caused by the accused in its repayment.

Further the punishment prescribed for the offence U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is imprisonment for a period which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque or with both.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, nature, year of the transaction,
nature of the instrument involved, cost of litigation and the rate of interest proposed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2012 (1) SCC 260 (R.Vijayan Vs Baby), I am of the opinion that it is just and desirable to impose fine of Rs.11,95,000/- and out of the said amount, it seems to be proper to award a sum of Rs.11,90,000/- as compensation to the C.C.No.54360/2015 complainant as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C and the remaining sum of Rs.5,000/- shall go to the State towards expenses.
With these observations, my findings on Point No.1 is in the Affirmative.
15. Point No.2:
In default, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for 6 months.

Out of the fine amount, Rs.5,000/-
shall be paid to the State towards expenses and remaining amount of Rs.11,90,000/- to the complainant as C.C.No.54360/2015 compensation as per the provisions of Sec.357(1) of Cr.P.C..

Further, it is made clear that in  view of proviso to Sec.421(1) of  Cr.P.C, the accused would not be  absolved from her liability to pay  compensation amount of Rs.11,90,000/- awarded u/s. 357 of Cr.P.C. even if she undergoes the default sentence.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Pursuant to the approach made by the accused, the complainant with an intention to help the accused to improve their business had paid a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- to the accused in the second week of February 2015.
Pursuant to receipt of the amount as aforesaid and inspite of lapse of three months as agreed, the accused failed and neglected to repay the amount payable to the complainant and as such, having no other alternative the complainant voluntarily approached the accused and requested to repay the amount payable.
Upon such request, the accused on one pretext or the other had been escaping from her liability, thereafter on persistent demands made by the complainant, the accused in discharge of her debt and liability issued a cheque bearing No.030389 dated 03.06.2015 drawn on Vijaya Bank, K.R. Puram Branch, Bengaluru-560036 and thereby promised and assured the complainant that the said cheque would C.C.No.54360/2015 be duly honored on the date of its presentation.
The complainant presented the said cheque for encashment on 08.06.2015 through her banker Vijaya Bank, K.R. Puram Branch, Bengaluru-560036, but it came to be dishonored for the reason "funds insufficient" vide endorsement dated 11.06.2015.
Thereafter,
the complainant issued legal notice on 24.06.2015 to the accused calling upon the accused to pay the cheque amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further it is not the case of the accused that the cheque in question does not pertain to her account.
Such being the case, it is relevant to mention here that when the accused has admitted the issuance of the cheque and her signature on it, the initial presumption as contemplated U/S 139 of the N.I Act has to be raised by the court in favour of the complainant, however the accused is entitled to rebut the said presumptions as held in the case of Sri Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan by the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in AIR 2010 SC 1898.
. Once the presumption U/S 139 and 118 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is raised, it is for the accused to rebut the said presumption by adducing cogent evidence in support of his defence.
If for a moment the story of the accused for failure to take any legal action against the complainant in view of the threatenings made by the complainant and her family members is believed, what prevented the accused to take any legal action against the complainant from the date of the reply notice as stated in para.14 of the reply notice at Ex.P14 till this day cannot be ascertained and the reasons are best known to the accused herself.
Making firm denial of the case of the complainant and issuance of reply notice at the earliest point of time itself is not sufficient to believe the defence of the accused for the discussion made above.
Merely because the complainant had filed the above said two complaints and has filed the present complaint against the accused is not sufficient to hold that the complainant had no financial capacity to lend the alleged money since it is the defence of the accused only that she had subscribed a chit of Rs.5,00,000/- with her and no prudent man would subscribe a chit for such a higher amount when the person conducting the chit has no financial capacity C.C.No.54360/2015 to pay it.
Merely because the complainant did not produce the I.T.R. pertaining to her husband and that her husband has not shown the above said transaction of sale in his I.T.R. is not sufficient to hold that the complainant had no financial capacity to pay the alleged money to the accused.
Further the non production of the chit in which the complainant stated that she might have made a writing for having lent the alleged money to the accused is also not a ground to believe the entire defence of the accused as it is not the case of the accused that she had executed any such writings in C.C.No.54360/2015 favour of the complainant.
From the above discussion, it is crystal clear that the accused even failed to prove her defence that the complainant had no financial capacity to lend the alleged money to the accused at the relevant point of time.
As such, considering the entire materials on record, in my opinion,
the accused has failed to rebut the presumptions available in favour of the complainant by adducing cogent oral and documentary evidence and even to raise a probable defence and on the other hand, I am of the opinion that the complainant has proved her case beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused has committed offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the C.C.No.54360/2015 accused has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
14.
Further the punishment prescribed for the offence U/s.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is imprisonment for a period which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque or with both.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, nature, year of the transaction,
nature of the instrument involved, cost of litigation and the rate of interest proposed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2012 (1) SCC 260 (R.Vijayan Vs Baby), I am of the opinion that it is just and desirable to impose fine of Rs.11,95,000/- and out of the said amount, it seems to be proper to award a sum of Rs.11,90,000/- as compensation to the C.C.No.54360/2015 complainant as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C and the remaining sum of Rs.5,000/- shall go to the State towards expenses.
15. Point No.2:
In view of my findings on Point No.1, I proceed to pass following;
O R D E R Acting u/s. 255(2) of Cr.P.C., the accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable u/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881.
The accused is hereby sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.11,95,000/-.
In default, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for 6 months.
Out of the fine amount, Rs.5,000/-
shall be paid to the State towards expenses and remaining amount of Rs.11,90,000/- to the complainant as C.C.No.54360/2015 compensation as per the provisions of Sec.357(1) of Cr.P.C..
Further, it is made clear that in  view of proviso to Sec.421(1) of  Cr.P.C, the accused would not be  absolved from her liability to pay  compensation amount of Rs.11,90,000/- awarded u/s. 357 of Cr.P.C. even if she undergoes the default sentence.
The bail bond and cash security of the accused stand hereby continued till the appeal period is over.
Office is directed to furnish free copy of this judgment to the accused forthwith.
